# Kubera walks into a finance, wealth & commerce firm

Walk into any finance, wealth & commerce outfit and watch for ten minutes. You will see a very old act performed with newer props. The act has a name. It is **Kubera**.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Lord of Laṅkā Before Rāvaṇa.** Kubera built the golden city of Laṅkā on the world’s far shore, served by the yakṣas and filled with his hoard.  His half-brother Rāvaṇa, through austerities and violence, took the city and the flying chariot Pushpaka from him; Kubera withdrew north to mount Gandhamādana, and Laṅkā passed to the demons — the great city’s golden age remembered as his.

**The Aerial Car Pushpaka.** The epic’s greatest vehicle belonged to Kubera: the self-moving palace-car Pushpaka, won back from Rāvaṇa by Rāma and returned in the epic’s closing book to its maker’s friend.  To ride Pushpaka is to command the wealth of the world from above — and Rāma, refusing it, set the moral: treasure serves, the righteous decline it.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Finance, Wealth & Commerce

*The treasurer of the gods, regent of the north — wealth's oldest named guardian.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Gems, Jewelry & Luxury Materials

*Lord of riches and the nine treasures — the gem-vaults of mythology are his accounting.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Retail & Marketplaces

*Lord of riches — the marketplace as his counting-house, the merchant's divine patron.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

## Not the First Rebrand

Kubera is Vaiśravaṇa in Buddhist lands, Jambhala in Tibet, and the model of every treasurer-god from the yakṣa-cults to the Japanese Bishamonten — the same northern regent under three names.  The Greeks heard Plutus in him; the comparatists hear the Celtic Dagda’s cauldron in his inexhaustible pot. The office is only the latest translation.
